result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Validate.assert_dimension_scores()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: >- Raise an AssertionError if any dimension's health score falls below a minimum. twitter-card: title: >- [Validate.assert_dimension_scores()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: >- Raise an AssertionError if any dimension's health score falls below a minimum. title: >- [Validate.assert_dimension_scores()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Raise an AssertionError if any dimension's health score falls below a minimum. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Raise an `AssertionError` if any dimension's health score falls below a minimum. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/validate.py#L20370-L20484){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Validate.assert_dimension_scores( thresholds=None, message=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The `assert_dimension_scores()` method checks each data quality dimension's score (from [`get_dimension_scores()`](`pointblank.Validate.get_dimension_scores`)) against a minimum acceptable value. This is useful in automated testing and CI environments where you want to fail the run when, say, the completeness score drops below `95`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [thresholds]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A mapping of dimension name to a minimum acceptable score (`0`-`100`). If `None`, the minimums set via [`config(dimension_thresholds=...)`](`pointblank.config`) are used. A dimension present in the thresholds but absent from the validation is ignored. [message]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Custom error message to use if the assertion fails. If `None`, a default message that lists the offending dimensions (with actual vs. required scores) is generated. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [AssertionError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any dimension's score is below its specified minimum. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's validate the `small_table` dataset with a not-null check (a completeness step) and a range check (a validity step). ::: {#2780818a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb small_table = pb.load_dataset(dataset="small_table", tbl_type="polars") validation = ( pb.Validate(data=small_table) .col_vals_not_null(columns="c") .col_vals_gt(columns="d", value=1000) .interrogate() ) validation.get_dimension_scores() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'completeness': 84.62, 'validity': 53.85} ``` ::: ::: Requiring completeness of at least 80 and validity of at least 50 passes, so nothing happens: ::: {#e634b38f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} validation.assert_dimension_scores(thresholds={"completeness": 80, "validity": 50}) ``` ::: Raising the completeness minimum to 95 makes the assertion fail. The `AssertionError` is caught here so that its message can be shown: ::: {#01236b8c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} try: validation.assert_dimension_scores(thresholds={"completeness": 95, "validity": 50}) except AssertionError as e: print(e) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Dimension health score(s) below the required minimum: completeness (84.62% < 95%) ``` ::: ::: The message lists each dimension below its minimum, with the actual and required scores. In a test suite or a CI job, leave the error uncaught so that it fails the run. To use the same minimums everywhere, set them once with `config(dimension_thresholds=...)` and call `assert_dimension_scores()` without `thresholds=`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~Validate.get_dimension_scores`) : Get the scores without raising. [](`~config`) : Set default per-dimension thresholds globally.
